testCase.title: Plumbing fixtures for an accessory assembly space

projectContext.potentialClassification: Group B under the accessory assembly provision

exactPassages: A room or space used for assembly purposes with an occupant load of fewer than 75 persons and accessory to another occupancy shall be classified as a Group B occupancy or as part of that occupancy, except that the number of plumbing fixtures for such a room or space is permitted to be calculated in accordance with the requirements for assembly occupancies.

Plumbing fixtures shall be provided for the type of occupancy and in the minimum number shown in Table 403.1. Types of occupancies not shown in Table 403.1 shall be considered individually by the commissioner. The number of occupants shall be determined by the New York City Building Code. Occupancy classification shall be determined in accordance with the New York City Building Code.

The number of fixtures for building or nonaccessory tenant space used for assembly purposes by fewer than 75 persons and classified as Group B occupancy in accordance with Section 303.1, Exception 2 of the New York City Building Code shall be permitted to be calculated in accordance with the requirements for Assembly occupancies.

To determine the occupant load of each sex, the total occupant load shall be divided in half. To determine the required number of fixtures, the fixture ratio or ratios for each fixture type shall be applied to the occupant load of each sex in accordance with Table 403.1. Fractional numbers resulting from applying the fixture ratios of Table 403.1 shall be rounded up to the next whole number. For calculations involving multiple occupancies, such fractional numbers for each occupancy shall first be summed and then rounded up to the next whole number. Fixture calculations in Group B office occupancies shall utilize the total occupant load on a given floor to determine the number of fixtures required for that floor.
Exception: The total occupant load shall not be required to be divided in half where approved statistical data indicates a distribution of the sexes of other than 50 percent of each sex.

testCase.question: If the multipurpose room is permitted to be classified as Group B because it has fewer than 75 occupants, can its required plumbing fixtures be calculated using the normal Group B fixture requirements?
testCase.expectedConclusion: Not automatically. Although an accessory assembly space with fewer than 75 occupants may be classified as Group B or as part of the occupancy it serves, the code permits the plumbing fixtures for that assembly use to be calculated using the applicable Assembly fixture requirements. The appropriate assembly category must first be identified from the room's actual use. The total occupant load is generally divided equally between the sexes unless approved statistical information supports another distribution. Fixture ratios are then applied, fractions are combined as required for multiple occupancies, and the resulting fractions are rounded up. A final fixture count requires the calculated occupant load, applicable assembly use, existing shared facilities, and other relevant project conditions.

answer.conclusion: Not necessarily. A qualifying accessory assembly multipurpose room with an occupant load of fewer than 75 persons is classified as Group B (or as part of its accessory occupancy), but the selected Building Code provision expressly permits its plumbing-fixture count to be calculated under the Assembly-occupancy requirements instead. The selected Plumbing Code language likewise permits Assembly fixture calculations for a qualifying under-75-person assembly space classified as Group B. Thus, normal Group B fixture requirements may be the applicable baseline based on the Group B classification, but the selected provisions provide a specific permission to use Assembly requirements; they do not establish that Group B fixture ratios must be used. [BC §303.1.3, Passage e4eb837e-309d-475d-8b7a-92ddd6243f0b; PC §403.1, Passage 0031d9db-393b-47a7-b0b3-f4a56351480f]
answer.explanation:
PC §403.1 requires fixtures by occupancy type and Table 403.1, with occupant load and occupancy classification determined under the NYC Building Code. For the room described, the relevant project-specific classification issue is whether it is an assembly-purpose room, accessory to another occupancy, with an occupant load below 75. If so, BC §303.1.3 classifies it as Group B or part of the accessory occupancy, while expressly allowing its fixture number to be calculated using Assembly requirements. The parallel PC provision also states that an under-75-person assembly building or nonaccessory tenant space classified as Group B under the cited Building Code exception is permitted to use Assembly requirements. [PC §403.1, Passage 23983c25-01eb-4d43-a7b4-f6b2103335e8; BC §303.1.3, Passage e4eb837e-309d-475d-8b7a-92ddd6243f0b; PC §403.1, Passage 0031d9db-393b-47a7-b0b3-f4a56351480f]

If a fixture calculation is performed, the selected procedure requires: (1) determine the total occupant load under the NYC Building Code; (2) ordinarily divide that load equally between sexes; (3) apply the applicable Table 403.1 fixture ratio(s) to each sex; and (4) round each resulting fractional fixture count up. For multiple occupancies, sum the fractional results for each occupancy before rounding up. The 50/50 sex split is not required where approved statistical data supports another distribution. A special floor-total rule applies to Group B office occupancies. [PC §403.1.1, Passages 85aca34d-08ef-412f-8701-32128b9408f2 and 059c4c69-d6a5-41de-976a-b7923f15eb64]
